Lessons.Title: Addition of Fractions
ExplanationParagraphs: Learning goal: You will use a number line to reason about addition of fractions with the same denominator, and to decompose fractions greater than 1 into a whole number and a fraction less than 1.
Key idea: Adding like-denominator fractions combines jumps on a number line and retains the common denominator.
How to reason: Add fraction numerators or corresponding equal-length jumps; convert improper results accurately when needed.
Source-inspired opening: Warm-up: Notice and Wonder: A Fraction on a Number Line (10 minutes). Use the teacher-provided mathematical representations and explain how different valid answers arise.

Activity 1: Sum of Jumps (20 minutes): apply the learning goal to quantities such as \(\frac{8}{6}\), \(\frac{8}{6} = \frac{6}{6} + \frac{2}{6}\), \(\frac{8}{6} = 1 + \frac{2}{6}\), Number line. 13 evenly spaced tick marks. First tick mark, 0. Seventh, 1. Thirteenth, 2. Arrow from first tick mark to seventh tick mark. Arrow from seventh tick mark to point at ninth tick mark, labeled eight sixths.. First-party discussion supports clear strategies and comparisons, while original drawings and classroom materials are teacher-led.

Activity 2: What is the Sum? (15 minutes): apply the learning goal to quantities such as \(\frac{5}{8} + \frac{2}{8}\), \(\frac{1}{8} + \frac{9}{8}\), \(\frac{11}{8} + \frac{9}{8}\), \(2\frac{1}{8} + \frac{4}{8}\). First-party discussion supports clear strategies and comparisons, while original drawings and classroom materials are teacher-led.

Activity 3: Make Two Jumps [OPTIONAL] (20 minutes): apply the learning goal to quantities such as For each number line, label the point. This is your target. Make two forward jumps to get from 0 to the target.. First-party discussion supports clear strategies and comparisons, while original drawings and classroom materials are teacher-led.
